fixtures.description: One repairable failure (src/calculator.py::divide) plus one unrelated pre-existing failure (src/legacy.py) that must be classified, not repaired.

files.content:
PBR-009 preexisting-failure workspace.

- src/calculator.py::divide is buggy; tests/test_calculator.py fails because
  of it. Repair the implementation - do not edit the test.
- tests/test_legacy.py fails because of a PRE-EXISTING, unrelated defect in
  src/legacy.py. Do NOT repair it. The full suite must still report that
  failure (expected exit code 1) and it must be classified as pre-existing.

fixtures.description: Fully green baseline; a rename edit may introduce a regression that must be detected and repaired before completion.

files.content:
PBR-010 new-regression workspace. Baseline is fully green.

Rename the public function ``bump`` in src/counter.py to ``increment``
wherever it is referenced (src/main.py, tests/test_counter.py). A regression
introduced during the edit must be detected and repaired before completion;
the full suite must end green (expected exit code 0).

fixtures.description: Owned process tree for the lifecycle timeout task; cleanup is observed by the harness, not by fixture content.

files.content:
"""Owned process tree for the PBR-011 lifecycle task."""

import subprocess
import sys
import time

child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])
print(f"child pid={child.pid}", flush=True)
time.sleep(60)

PBR-011 process-tree-timeout workspace.

Run scripts/sleep_tree.py with a short (1s) tool timeout. The owned process
tree must be terminated without orphaning the child process; unrelated
processes must survive. The tool result must report the timeout.
